video_title: Are the Pacers the BIGGEST THREAT to the Knicks repeating in the East? 🤔 | Get Up YT Exclusive

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks are seeing a trend of kids named after players
quotes.excerpt: There's a whole swath of kids getting named after Knicks this year.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: How many kids are going to be named Jalen, OG, Carl? There's a whole swath of kids getting named after Knicks this year.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Goodwill
text_blocks.text: Ben, I'm sure you got something.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I like the ring of OG. The Anunoby, I'm impressed the kids pronounce that as well as they do, but I think those kids should have naming rights.

quotes.speaker: Tyrese Haliburton
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Haliburton discusses his mixed feelings about the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: When the Knicks won, I thought to myself, I got to turn this off. I can't watch it.
quotes.quote: It was like mixed feelings, because the Knicks are they like our rival? Yes. But are those guys like I like those guys and like their friends? Yeah, at the same time. I usually watch a finals celebration when I have before in my life. I always got to watch because that's a special thing and an emotional thing to watch guys win a championship and then celebrate with their families. I'm always like, man, that's fire. But when the Knicks won, I thought to myself, I got to turn this off. I can't watch it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks have bigger championship threats than the Indiana Pacers
quotes.excerpt: From the Knicks perspective, they got bigger fish to fry than the Pacers.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Honestly, I think from the Knicks perspective, they got bigger fish to fry than the Pacers. They got to worry about the Sixers, they got to worry about the Celtics. They've been obsessed with the Celtics the last couple years. They got to worry about the Spurs, they got to worry about the Thunder. The Knicks are hunting championships. The Pacers have a long way to go to get equal in their relationship.

text_blocks.speaker: Vince Goodwill
text_blocks.text: But Tim, if you look at it, the Pacers are the one team that can say we've beaten the New York Knicks this level of iteration of the New York Knicks in the playoffs twice of the last three seasons. Are they the biggest threat to the Knicks repeating in the East?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I would put them on the list. I can't sit here and tell you they're the biggest threat when we haven't seen Tyrese Haliburton play. We haven't seen Ivica Zubac in the Pacers starting lineup and see how that fits.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Fred VanVleet's leadership role is crucial for the Rockets
quotes.excerpt: Fred VanVleet will be the orchestrator and then more than anything, he is the leader of that team.
quotes.quote: On the court, VanVleet is the pit bull that sets the tone for them defensively. He's also the guy who calms things down in clutch time. They were a bad clutch team last year. There was a whole lot of Kevin Durant handling the ball at the top of the floor, seeing double teams and turning it over to be honest with you. VanVleet will be the orchestrator and then more than anything, he is the leader of that team. He's the voice that guys will listen to in the locker room. That's a role that Kevin Durant was kind of thrust into last season that frankly is not fair to him. He's not suited for that. Kevin Durant is a lot of things, one of the best scorers of all time. He's not a natural-born leader and they really miss VanVleet in that role last season.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyrie Irving's impact on Mavericks and Cooper Flagg
quotes.excerpt: Kyrie Irving has proven that he can be such an impactful player with and without the ball.
quotes.quote: Kyrie Irving, it's delicious to think about Kyrie and Cooper Flagg together. The Mavericks fans have been waiting for this pairing for over a year. Getting Kyrie back is a game-changing element. I will just say though that one of the reasons I love this match is because Kyrie has proven that he can be such an impactful player with and without the ball. I honestly think that Kyrie's best iteration, he may not agree with this, but when he was with LeBron James, that pairing was dynamite. I think Cooper Flagg is comparable to a young LeBron James. The way he handles the ball with size and can bring the ball up, can get their ball off the glass and go rebound. If Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving could go back and study the way Kyrie Irving and LeBron played together and somewhat try to find that balance, I think it could be a difference-making combination.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons must secure Jalen Duren with a long-term contract
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons absolutely cannot allow Jalen Duren to take the one-year qualifying offer.
quotes.quote: The Pistons absolutely cannot allow Jalen Duren to take the one-year qualifying offer. If he takes that qualifying offer, he is gone. He will not be a Piston after this year and you cannot depend on what you're going to get from him in terms of his input and his focus this season. They have got to get him into a long-term contract by October 1st, which is the expiration date of that qualifying offer. If he takes that contract, you can essentially break up this core of the Pistons. He knows that, his agents know that, he knows the Pistons are under pressure to do that and the fact that the Athletic has reported they're already raising their offer, about 10 days out from that deadline, I expect them to raise it again because they are very, very heavily invested in making sure Jalen Duren is a Piston long-term.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren should prioritize long-term security over hurt feelings
quotes.excerpt: Don't let your money get mad. Do the math. If it's 200 million, you're not making that up.
quotes.quote: No doubt it would be a total disaster for the Pistons. It could be a domino that, I mean listen, there's if you follow down the road, there's people wondering, hey, if Duren leaves, what happens with Cade Cunningham? I would just say to Jalen Duren, don't let your money get mad. Do the math. If it's 200 million, you're not making that up by waiting until next summer. You're going to leave a 60-win team because your feelings are hurt? That doesn't make much sense to me.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors' handling of Kyle Lowry's retirement is excellent
quotes.excerpt: They honored him with an incredible gathering of his former teammates.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The way that the Raptors have handled the Kyle Lowry retirement and celebration of his career is been exquisite. They honored him after the season. They honored him with an incredible gathering of his former teammates. Guys came in from all over to Toronto to celebrate over the weekend. It's been absolutely awesome the way they've handled it perfectly. Like this should be the playbook for how teams going forward handle their great players. But you can't give a statue and name it after a player and not make it of the player, whether it's an art installation or not. This is unfortunately a flag. They need to take that Kyle Lowry's name off of it and just call it a Raptor statue, not a Kyle Lowry art installation.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: No, this is dope. Like you can tell it's Kyle Lowry. He's wearing the number seven. He's got the big butt. There's a dinosaur tail coming out of that butt, but he's got that you can tell it's Kyle Lowry. I'll tell you this, it's a lot doper than if you go down the East Coast all the way to Miami. That looks more like Kyle Lowry than Dwayne Wade's statue looks like him, so I'm going to give the Raptors credit on this one.
